title: board v2 shell: one design system with light and dark themes and a visible toggle remembered per viewer, and a large voyage stage pinned under the top bar at every width that can shrink to a strip; existing regions and their rendering stay as they are
acceptance: Why. The captain reviewed four prototype rounds of the board on 2026-10-07 and approved the last one, verbatim: "看板樣式可以了, 可以以這個版本開發". Earlier notes from the captain, verbatim in substance: the page had no unity and too much text, the captain card needs the largest area, a dark mode toggle is needed, and the voyage game stays pinned at the top and larger. Later that day: "船員名冊顯示的太窄, 高度太限縮, 閱讀順序應該是先看意圖重點列表, 再帶到動畫邏輯帶看". The approved design is in the round's local brief (firstmate records state/briefs/T-241.design.md for every round); its prototype code is reference only and holds no board data. Board v2 is split into three tasks: T-241 the shell, T-245 the captain card, T-246 the sheets.

Change 1, tokens and themes. A new board/public/board.css, linked from index.html after the inline <style>, defines these tokens. Light palette (html[data-theme=light]): --chart #EEF2F0, --hull #FFFFFF, --hull2 #F6F8F7, --harbour #10233B, --fog #5B6B7A, --line #CBD5D2, --signal #F2B90F, --flag-red #C2372C, --flag-blue #1D4F91, --kelp #2F7D5B. Dark palette (html[data-theme=dark]): --chart #0E1824, --hull #16222F, --hull2 #1C2A39, --harbour #E6EDF1, --fog #93A3B1, --line #26384A, --signal #F0B429, --flag-red #E35D4F, --flag-blue #6EA8E8, --kelp #4FB286. Type scale tokens --t13 … --t41 (13, 15, 17, 21, 26, 33, 41 px), spacing --s1 … --s7 (4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48 px), radius --r-chip 4px and --r-panel 8px. Under each theme it maps index.html's existing custom properties onto them: --bg→--chart, --bg2→--hull, --bg3→--hull2, --line→--line, --fg→--harbour, --fg2 and --fg3→--fog, --brass→--signal, --ok→--kelp, --bad→--flag-red, --accent→--flag-blue; every other existing variable (for example --warn, --wait, --mono, --sans) keeps its value. So every rule that reads those variables follows the theme. Light-theme legibility, by tokens first (the dark theme and ship.css stay byte-identical; ship.css keeps its brass literal for tests/ship.spec.ts). Under html[data-theme=light] board.css redefines the accent variables used as text colour to light values, each with its WCAG ratio on #FFFFFF / #EEF2F0 / #F6F8F7: --brass #7A5600 (6.65 / 5.89 / 6.23), --warn #8A4B00 (6.80 / 6.02 / 6.38), --wait #6B2FA0 (8.27 / 7.32 / 7.75), --ok #1E6B47 (6.46 / 5.72 / 6.06), --bad #B3261E (6.54 / 5.79 / 6.13), --accent #1D4F91 (8.14 / 7.21 / 7.63); --fg is --harbour and --fg2 and --fg3 are --fog (#5B6B7A: 5.48 / 4.86 / 5.14). The kind badges (--k-* backgrounds with #080f17 text) and the pressed buttons (#1d4b7a with #fff) keep their colours in both themes. Text whose colour is a hard-coded literal gets one light-theme rule set in board.css instead of per-selector patches: (a) the crew roster: every descendant of .roster and .rosterbar uses color var(--fg2), with var(--fg) for .roster .nm, .roster .jb .tt, .roster h4.rgroup and the .rl/.pj/.rd/.rv/.rm/.rc cells, var(--bad) for .rv.warn and .rm.warn, and background var(--bg3) for the elements that hard-code a dark translucent background (.roster .rhead, .roster h3 .rgroupbtn, .rosterbar .toggle), pressed buttons excepted; (b) the rest: `.counts` gets the shorthand `background:var(--hull)`, which removes its dark gradient image, `.counts span` and `#merging li` use var(--fg2), `.vend.x`, `.pchip` and `#merging li.unknown` use var(--warn), `#pcount` uses color #FFFFFF on its --wait background (8.27:1), `#gl`'s inline colour follows --brass, now light-safe, with no override; and the two elements that keep a dark or gold gradient background in light keep text that reads on it: `html[data-theme=light] .capstage .lbl` uses color #d9a441 (the dark-theme brass, 8.33:1 on #140f22) and `.capstage .lbl span` keeps its #8b7aa8 (4.9:1 on #140f22), because the portrait box keeps its dark gradient in both themes, and `.acts .go` keeps its #2a1c05 text on its gold gradient; `html[data-theme=light] .acts .opt` and `html[data-theme=light] .acts .opt:disabled` use color var(--fg) (colour only, no border or background change), because the decision options set no text colour and a read-only board disables them, which Chromium draws in its default faint grey (1.99:1 on the light background); captain card D-firstmate-workflow-T241-4 adds this rule. Stated exceptions that stay exactly as they are: hard-coded colours in the inline <style> that no variable reaches (for example #3a2a52, #7c322b, #26323d) and the existing .task-detail box-shadow; board.css itself adds no box-shadow. The inline <style> in index.html is unchanged except for the voyage rules of Change 3. board/public/ship.css is not edited: it keeps its literal brass hex values and every rule tests/ship.spec.ts pins (the .acts rules, #orderFeedback, the .change-fallback rules, the page-wide reduced-motion rule and the brass-only accent check), and it follows the theme through the var() names it already uses.

Change 2, the theme toggle. `data-theme` is set on the <html> element. A new board/public/board.js, loaded after the existing scripts, sets it on load from localStorage key board.theme, or from prefers-color-scheme when no key is stored; every storage read and write is inside try/catch, so a page whose storage throws still renders and toggles for the session. A button `#themeToggle` is added to the top bar (.top, before #langs); this is the one markup change outside the voyage panel. It is a 32x32px icon button (a half-filled circle glyph, no visible text, font-size fixed in px) with flex:none. At 320px wide .top already wraps (flex-wrap:wrap, index.html:136-137); the button sits on the same row as #langs and wraps with it, so the page still has no horizontal scroll, every visible .langs button stays inside the viewport, and tests/e2e/board-layout.spec.ts's 320px checks (lines ~148-151, including the doubled-font check) pass unchanged; the new shell test repeats the 320px no-scroll and .langs-inside checks with the default font size doubled. Its aria-label and title come from index.html's chrome(), which already relabels the header on every language switch, through a double-quoted t("themeToggle") call that the existing i18n key lint reads; the key `themeToggle` is in both dictionaries. board.js holds no Han characters and calls no t(). Storage safety in index.html's inline script, the only script edits of this task besides chrome()'s new line: the `localStorage.getItem("board.lang")` read at the language start-up and the `localStorage.setItem("board.lang", lang)` on a language switch are each wrapped in try/catch, so a page whose localStorage getItem and setItem throw renders, switches language for the session and toggles the theme, with or without ?lang=. The failure this covers is getItem/setItem throwing (Storage.prototype methods); a window.localStorage getter that itself throws is out of scope, and game.js's existing reads and writes are not changed for it.

Change 3, the voyage stage. game.js keeps mounting #voyage with `#counts.before(panel)` and keeps its homes, its drawer, its full mode, its Escape handling and its keys (board.voyage.hidden in localStorage, board.voyage.mode in sessionStorage). In index.html's inline `@media(max-width:650px)` block exactly two rules change: `body>#voyage{order:1}` is removed, so #voyage keeps its DOM place under the top bar above every card at every width, and `#voyage-stage{height:330px}` becomes `height:270px` (used when the viewer expanded the stage); the block's other rules stay (body{display:flex;flex-direction:column}, the order:2 rules for #shipregion, .lanes-wrap and .logwrap, and the two .voyage-full grid rules that keep full mode working at narrow widths). Above 650px #voyage-stage is clamp(270px, 36vh, 440px) high (the existing 420px rule changes to that). game.js adds one button `#voyage-size` to #voyage-bar that shrinks the stage to an 88px strip (72px at 650px and below) and back; the choice is stored in localStorage key board.voyage.size as the string 'strip' or 'full-size' inside try/catch and restored on load. With nothing stored, the size follows the viewport live: game.js listens to matchMedia('(max-width:650px)') and shows the strip while it matches and full-size while it does not, on load and on every resize, until the viewer presses #voyage-size, which stores the choice and stops the live switching. The new write goes through game.js's existing put() helper. Pixel budget at 650px and below with nothing stored: the panel takes at most 160px (12px top margin, 1px border, the 60px button bar, the 72px strip, 1px border, 12px bottom margin), so the first .dcard still starts above y=844 at 390x844 and 650x844 as tests/e2e/game.spec.ts (the 650/390 loop) and tests/e2e/board-continuation.spec.ts (390x844) require today; those two assertions are unchanged. The strip applies only in panel mode: it is a class `voyage-strip` on #voyage whose rule is written as `#voyage.voyage-strip:not(.voyage-full *) #voyage-stage` and is overridden by `.voyage-full #voyage-stage{height:100%}` (board.css repeats that full-mode rule after the strip rule), so full mode always fills the screen; #voyage-size is an icon button (no visible text, so the bar stays one row at 390px) with its label as aria-label and title, and it is shown only in panel mode and is hidden in full mode and while the voyage is hidden. Its label uses the keys `voyageShrink` and `voyageGrow` through game.js's existing label() function, so it relabels on a language switch exactly as voyageWorkflow does (VOYAGE.update passes the new t); both keys are in both dictionaries, and tests/board.test.sh's voyage label list gains them. The full mode and the hidden mode work as today. prefers-reduced-motion turns off the size transition.

Not changed, stated. board/server.ts and every API, the event pipeline, card generators and copy, the voyage game under board/public/voyage2d, ship.js, ship.css, every region's markup and rendering (counts, deck, roster, lanes, history, log, task detail) except the one top-bar button of Change 2, and every id. The captain card is T-245; the sheets are T-246.

Tests, new behaviour (fail on base, pass after). tests/e2e/board-v2-shell.spec.ts: for each theme, getComputedStyle(document.documentElement) returns every palette value above for --chart, --hull, --hull2, --harbour, --fog, --line, --signal, --flag-red, --flag-blue and --kelp, and --bg resolves to --chart's value; the toggle switches html[data-theme] and the choice survives a reload; with no stored key an emulated dark colour scheme renders dark and light renders light; with Storage.prototype.getItem and setItem made to throw, a page loaded without ?lang= renders, switches language and toggles, and #voyage is present; after switching the language to zh-TW, #themeToggle and #voyage-size show the zh-TW labels; at 1440x900 the #voyage-stage height is at least 270px and at most 440px; #voyage-size shrinks it to the strip height and the choice survives a reload; with nothing stored, both when loaded at 390x844 and when loaded at 1440x900 and then resized to 650 and to 390, #voyage sits above the first .dcard, its stage is the 72px strip, the panel is at most 160px high and the first .dcard starts above y=844; after pressing #voyage-size there the stage is 270px high, and it stays full-size (never the strip) across a resize to 1440x900, where it is clamp(270px, 36vh, 440px) = 324px high, and back to 390, where it is 270px again; at 320 wide there is no horizontal scroll and every visible .langs button is inside the viewport; full mode at 390 wide still lays out as today; #voyage-size is hidden while the voyage is hidden; with board.voyage.size='strip' stored, entering full mode fills the viewport and #voyage-size is hidden there, and leaving it returns to the strip; 1440 and 390 widths have no horizontal page scroll in both themes; in the light theme at 1440x900 and at 390x844, on a fixture with a waiting count, an engine label, a pending dispatch and a pending merge card, an expanded strip, a crew roster with a header, groups and a warning row, and a log with a greenlit line, a sweep checks every visible element with a non-empty own text node inside .top, #readOnly, .counts, #deckwrap (the cards and strips), #shipregion (the roster) and .logwrap (the log): its computed text colour has a WCAG contrast ratio of at least 4.5 against its effective background, computed by walking from the element itself up to the root and compositing every background colour with alpha onto the ones beneath, starting from the page background; an element or ancestor whose computed background-image is not none counts as an unknown background, and the element is checked instead by a fixed pair: .capstage .lbl text against #140f22 and .acts .go text against #b8862c, plus .capstage .lbl span against #140f22, each at least 4.5:1, and any other element over a background image fails the test. The fixture's roster holds no queued row, because queued rows are dimmed by opacity on purpose in both themes and the sweep does not model opacity. Excluded, listed: everything inside the voyage iframe and #voyage-bar, the diagram iframes, the kind badges (.k-*), and pressed buttons; and getComputedStyle under light returns the light token values listed in Change 1.

Tests, updated and regression. tests/e2e/game.spec.ts changes only two things: its narrow-width order check (line ~281): at 650 and 390 wide #voyage now sits above the first .dcard instead of below it, still above .lanes-wrap; and its board read allowlist (the `reads` set near line 196) adds exactly '/board.css' and '/board.js', the two new board assets; the voyage-frame allowlist at line 45 stays unchanged. tests/board.test.sh adds voyageShrink and voyageGrow to its voyage label list. tests/e2e/board-continuation.spec.ts (its 390x844 first-card check), tests/e2e/board-layout.spec.ts (its 320px checks), tests/ship.spec.ts, tests/board-chips.test.sh, tests/i18n.test.sh and every other e2e spec pass unchanged.
Migration. Display only. A viewer with no board.theme follows the system scheme; board.voyage.hidden and board.voyage.mode keep working.

Docs. design/design.md §8 'The captain's board': edit in place for the themes and palettes, the toggle and the stage size; and in its '### T-125: Live voyage seam' subsection replace the sentence 'On screens at most 650px wide the panel follows the decisions and precedes the lanes; desktop retains the panel above the decisions.' with one saying the panel sits above the decisions at every width. And in §5.2, where the five card defaults are listed (around line 440), replace the fifth default 'and provide no light theme' with a sentence recording that the captain's approval of the board prototype on 2026-10-07 ('看板樣式可以了, 可以以這個版本開發') added a light theme and a per-viewer toggle, with dark kept as the first-visit theme when the system scheme is dark.
